200	EM ranks first across all four tested conditional configurations---SciERC NER ($\rho{=}0.360$), CoNLL Qwen $N{=}16$ ($\rho{=}0.466$), CoNLL LLaMA 3-seed ($\rho{=}0.462$), and SciERC RE ($\rho{=}0.417$)---despite full-set rankings ranging from \#1 (CoNLL Qwen) to \#5 (SciERC RE).
201	On the full set, EM is diluted by trivial agreement: instances where all $N$ samples produce identical (possibly incorrect) outputs receive EM${=}1$ regardless of quality, compressing the signal's dynamic range.
202	On the conditional set---where the model demonstrably produces varied outputs---exact agreement becomes the strongest quality signal.
203	The margin over SJ is largest on RE ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.171$), where compound extraction decisions amplify output variability, and smallest on CoNLL LLaMA ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.002$), where all signals converge near $\rho{\approx}0.46$.
204	
205	\paragraph{WNUT-17 full signal analysis.}
206	Table~\ref{tab:wnut} (\S\ref{sec:qe_results}) reports all five signals on WNUT-17 with full-set and conditional $\rho$.
207	The full-set $p$-values are: VC ${<}$1e-112, FK $p{=}0.001$, SJ $p{=}0.020$, EM $p{=}0.194$, LP ${<}$1e-28.
208	VC's high full-set $\rho{=}0.724$ is entirely driven by the zero/non-zero boundary (conditional $\rho{=}0.038$, $p{=}0.49$), while LP's conditional $\rho{=}0.350$ is the highest among all signals on the non-zero subset, confirming that full-set correlations on high-failure-rate datasets conflate binary success prediction with quality gradation.
209	
210	\paragraph{Cross-configuration selection analysis.}
211	Table~\ref{tab:cross_selection} extends the selection analysis to four additional configurations.
212	On LLaMA SciERC, where output diversity remains substantial (18\% identical outputs, 39\% unique), LP achieves the highest selection F1 (0.652) at $N{=}8$ but still falls within bootstrap noise of single-sample (0.646), replicating the gap observed on Qwen SciERC (Table~\ref{tab:selection}).
213	On CoNLL, 57--88\% of instances produce identical outputs across all $N$ samples, reflecting a ceiling effect (single-sample F1 ${\approx}$0.91--0.92) rather than signal failure; selection analysis on these configurations is uninformative because there is little per-sample variance for any signal to exploit.
214	
215	\begin{table*}[t]
216	\centering
217	\small
218	\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection F1 (macro, instance-averaged) across configurations ($T{=}1.0$). Best non-oracle signal per row in \textbf{bold}. At $N{=}8$, no signal significantly outperforms greedy in any configuration. At $N{=}16$ on LLaMA CoNLL, VC achieves small but significant gains ($+0.28$~pp, $p{<}0.03$; see text below). CoNLL shows especially tight clustering where greedy already exceeds 0.90.}

232	\paragraph{Diminishing returns of $N$-scaling.}
233	Our $N{=}8$ and $N{=}16$ comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:robustness}) characterize the marginal value of additional samples for test-time scaling \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2025scaling}.
234	For quality estimation, structural signals benefit consistently but sublinearly: SJ $\rho$ improves by $+0.047$ (Qwen SciERC, 3-seed mean) and $+0.032$ (LLaMA CoNLL, 3-seed mean) when doubling from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$, while log-probability is approximately $N$-invariant ($\Delta\rho{\leq}0.021$).
235	Structural signals leverage $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise comparisons (28 pairs at $N{=}8$, 120 at $N{=}16$), but the $\rho$ improvement is far less than proportional, indicating diminishing information per additional comparison.
236	This asymmetry gives structural signals a relative advantage in the compute-constrained regime: at $N{=}8$, SJ already achieves $\rho{=}0.431$ on LLaMA CoNLL (vs.\ LP $\rho{=}0.307$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.124$), and the gap \textit{widens} at $N{=}16$ ($\Delta{=}{+}0.163$) because structural signals continue to benefit from additional pairwise evidence while LP does not.
237	For sample selection, additional samples increase the oracle upper bound---more draws raise the probability of a high-quality candidate---but signal-based selection remains flat because the selector's inability to identify the best candidate is a granularity limitation, not a sample size limitation.
238	The practical implication is that $N{=}8$ captures most of the achievable quality estimation benefit; further scaling widens rather than closes the correlation-selection gap absent stronger per-sample selectors.
239	
240	\paragraph{$N{=}16$ CoNLL selection: small but significant.}
241	While quality estimation benefits sublinearly from $N$-scaling, selection behavior at $N{=}16$ reveals a nuanced exception on LLaMA CoNLL.
242	VC achieves the largest gain over single-sample ($+0.28$~pp, $p{=}0.003$--$0.027$ across 3 seeds, all significant), with SJ, FK, and EM at $+0.22$--$0.23$~pp and LP at $+0.12$~pp (2/3 seeds significant).
243	These gains are statistically significant but practically minimal: oracle headroom at $N{=}16$ is only 2.5~pp, so VC captures approximately 10\% of the available headroom.
244	This reinforces the primary finding: even under the most favorable conditions---high baseline performance, more candidates, and aggregated multi-seed evidence---signal-based selection recovers only a fraction of the oracle headroom available.
245

249	The SJ--LP gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.155$) is clearly significant, confirming the structural advantage reported in \S\ref{sec:qe_results}.
250	The VC--SJ gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.019$) is not significant, indicating that these two structural signals perform comparably.
251	The SJ--EM gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.065$) is borderline significant, with the CI lower bound at $+0.003$ and upper bound at $+0.130$.

290	\section{Diversity and Selection Analysis}\label{app:diversity}
291	
292	\begin{figure*}[t]
293	\centering
294	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_selection_gap}
295	\caption{The correlation-selection gap on SciERC NER ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$, 2-seed mean). Bars show best-of-$N$ selection F1; the line marks quality estimation $\rho$. Despite $\rho$ up to 0.40, no signal significantly outperforms single-sample (all $p{>}0.05$; Table~\ref{tab:selection}). Dashed line indicates oracle upper bound. RE selection results in Table~\ref{tab:selection}.}
296	\label{fig:selection_gap}
297	\end{figure*}
298	
299	\paragraph{Output diversity quantification.}
300	Table~\ref{tab:diversity} summarizes output diversity across configurations.
301	On SciERC, output diversity is substantial: Qwen produces 43\% unique outputs per instance (mean 3.5 distinct out of $N{=}8$), with per-sample F1 standard deviation of 0.144 and mean pairwise SJ of 0.703.
302	LLaMA shows similar diversity (39\% unique, F1 std 0.11).
303	On CoNLL, diversity collapses: 57\% (Qwen) to 88\% (LLaMA) of instances produce identical outputs across all $N$ samples, reflecting a ceiling effect where single-sample F1 already exceeds 0.90.
304	WNUT-17 shows 55\% identical outputs, driven by the 52\% zero-F1 rate.
305	
306	\begin{table}[t]
307	\centering
308	\small
309	\caption{Output diversity across configurations ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). ``Identical'' = fraction of instances with all $N$ outputs identical. ``Unique'' = mean fraction of distinct outputs per instance.}
310	\label{tab:diversity}
311	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
312	\toprule
313	Config & Identical & Unique \\
314	\midrule
315	Qwen/SciERC & 11\% & 43\% \\
316	LLaMA/SciERC & 18\% & 39\% \\
317	Qwen/CoNLL & 57\% & --- \\
318	LLaMA/CoNLL & 88\% & --- \\

324	\paragraph{Oracle-improvable fraction.}
325	Across SciERC configurations, 39--42\% of instances contain at least one sample with F1 exceeding single-sample\footnote{Oracle-improvable and diversity-stratified analyses use $n{=}529$ (excluding instances with empty gold annotations; see \S\ref{sec:evaluation}); the diversity quantification in Table~\ref{tab:diversity} uses the full test set.}: Qwen NER 42.0\% (222/529, mean headroom $+$31.9~pp among improvable instances), Qwen RE 41.3\% (164/397, $+$45.3~pp), LLaMA NER 39.3\% (208/529, $+$33.7~pp).
326	On CoNLL, only 4--9\% of instances are improvable, confirming the ceiling effect.
327	
328	\paragraph{Diversity-stratified selection gap.}
329	On the 44\% of Qwen SciERC instances with high diversity (${\geq}4$ unique outputs among 8 samples, $n{=}232$), oracle headroom reaches $+$16.3~pp, yet all consistency-based signals (SJ, FK, EM, VC) select at or below single-sample, and LP---the only per-sample signal---achieves merely $+$0.8~pp.
330	LLaMA replicates this pattern: on its high-diversity subset ($n{=}186$), oracle headroom reaches $+$20.1~pp while consistency signals remain at or below single-sample and LP captures only $+$2.0~pp.
331	This rules out insufficient diversity as an explanation for the correlation-selection gap.
332	
333	\paragraph{TOST equivalence testing.}\label{app:tost}
334	The primary evidence against selection gains comes from effect sizes and confidence intervals: Cohen's $d{=}0.038$ for the best signal (NER LP) and bootstrap 95\% CI [$-$3.0, $+$4.2]~pp spanning zero.
335	Table~\ref{tab:tost} supplements this with two one-sided tests (TOST), testing whether each signal's selection F1 is equivalent to single-sample within a bound $\delta$.
336	The $\delta$ values are contextualized against oracle headroom (12--18~pp): $\delta{=}5$~pp corresponds to forgoing 28--38\% of the available headroom, $\delta{=}3$~pp forgoing 17--23\%, and $\delta{=}2$~pp less than 15\%.
337	These proportions use the same test data that defines the headroom, introducing circularity: $\delta$ is anchored to the very quantity it contextualizes.
338	We address this below with externally anchored equivalence margins.
339	The breakpoint $\delta^*$---the minimum equivalence margin at which each signal passes TOST---ranges from approximately 1.3~pp (SJ, ${\sim}$10\% of oracle headroom) to 3.4~pp (FK, ${\sim}$26\%) on NER, and from approximately 2.9~pp (LP, ${\sim}$16\%) to 6.5~pp (VC, ${\sim}$36\%) on RE.
340	On NER ($n{=}529$), at $\delta{=}{\pm}2$~pp, SJ and LP are confirmed equivalent to single-sample (TOST $p{<}0.05$); at $\delta{=}{\pm}3$~pp, four of five signals pass; at $\delta{=}{\pm}5$~pp, all five pass.
341	On RE ($n{=}397$, preliminary), EM and VC fail equivalence even at $\delta{=}{\pm}5$~pp due to systematic underperformance ($\Delta{=}{-}3.2$~pp and $-4.5$~pp respectively).
342	The effect sizes are negligible ($d{=}0.038$) and confidence intervals span zero, with TOST confirming equivalence at practically meaningful margins.

346	\small
347	\caption{TOST equivalence testing: signals vs.\ single-sample on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). \checkmark: equivalent at $p{<}0.05$; \texttimes: not equivalent. $\Delta$: mean F1 difference (signal $-$ single-sample).}

350	\toprule
351	& \multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{NER}} & \multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{RE}} \\

353	Signal & $\Delta$ & $\pm$2 & $\pm$3 & $\pm$5 & $\Delta$ & $\pm$2 & $\pm$3 & $\pm$5 \\

358	EM & $-$0.8 & \texttimes & \checkmark & \checkmark & $-$3.2 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \texttimes \\
359	VC & $-$1.0 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \checkmark & $-$4.5 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \texttimes \\
360	\bottomrule
361	\end{tabular}
362	\end{table}
363	
364	\paragraph{External equivalence margins.}
365	The oracle-headroom anchors above introduce circularity, as a reviewer correctly noted: $\delta$ is calibrated against the very quantity it contextualizes.
366	To resolve this, we supplement with three externally grounded margins:
367	(1) $\delta_{\mathrm{SEM}}$: the bootstrapped standard error of single-sample F1 (0.43--1.33~pp depending on configuration), representing measurement noise;
368	(2) $\delta_{\mathrm{practical}}{=}0.5$~pp, reflecting the threshold below which NER differences are considered negligible \cite{ratinov2009design};
369	(3) $\delta_{\mathrm{literature}}{=}1.0$~pp, the approximate significant-difference threshold established in NER evaluation methodology \cite{bergkirkpatrick2012empirical}.
370	
371	Results under these external anchors diverge sharply by configuration.
372	On LLaMA CoNLL ($n{=}2{,}756$), all signals pass equivalence at every $\delta$ ($p{<}0.001$), consistent with the near-zero selection deltas ($|\Delta|{\leq}0.1$~pp) and tight CIs at this sample size.
373	On Qwen CoNLL ($n{=}2{,}756$), no signal passes at any external $\delta$: selection F1 degrades by 0.9--1.5~pp relative to single-sample, exceeding even $\delta_{\mathrm{literature}}$.
374	On SciERC NER ($n{=}529$), only SJ passes at $\delta_{\mathrm{SEM}}{=}1.33$~pp (the widest SEM bound); all other signals and tighter margins fail.
375	These external anchors confirm that the equivalence conclusion is configuration-dependent: LLaMA CoNLL selection is robustly equivalent to single-sample under any reasonable margin, while SciERC and Qwen CoNLL selection shows detectable degradation at externally calibrated thresholds.
376	
377	\paragraph{Multiple comparison considerations.}\label{app:multiple_comparisons}
378	Our primary selection analysis involves ${\sim}$20 comparisons (5 signals $\times$ 3--4 configurations).
379	Since all primary selection results are non-significant ($p{>}0.05$), applying Benjamini-Hochberg correction can only make these results more conservative, strengthening the ``no signal beats greedy'' conclusion.
380	The sole positive finding---non-tied LP subset ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.004$; \S\ref{sec:discussion})---survives Bonferroni correction over 5 signal comparisons ($p_{\mathrm{adj}}{=}0.020 < 0.05$), as noted in the main text footnote.
381	For quality estimation signal rankings, differences between the top signals (e.g., VC vs.\ SJ on SciERC) should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as statistically confirmed orderings, given the limited power of 3-seed comparisons.
382	
383	\section{Multi-Seed Stability}\label{app:multiseed}
384	
385	Table~\ref{tab:multiseed} reports quality estimation metrics across three random seeds for both model families on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$).
386	On NER, the signal ranking VC${>}$SJ${>}$EM${>}$FK${>}$LP is identical across all six model-seed combinations, with $\sigma{\leq}0.025$ for all signals (rankings are stable across our 3 seeds, though statistical power with $n{=}3$ is limited).
387	On RE (Qwen only, preliminary), VC remains the top signal ($\rho{=}0.309{\pm}0.024$), but LP rises to \#2 ($\rho{=}0.297{\pm}0.022$), above FK, SJ, and EM---a reversal from the NER ranking that reflects RE's higher sensitivity to per-sample scoring.
388	LLaMA absolute values are systematically lower than Qwen on NER, consistent with the directionally-consistent-but-magnitude-dependent characterization in the main text.

413	\section{Training Configuration}\label{app:training}

EM ranks first across all four tested conditional configurations---SciERC NER ($\rho{=}0.360$), CoNLL Qwen $N{=}16$ ($\rho{=}0.466$), CoNLL LLaMA 3-seed ($\rho{=}0.462$), and SciERC RE ($\rho{=}0.417$)---despite full-set rankings ranging from \#1 (CoNLL Qwen) to \#5 (SciERC RE).
On the full set, EM is diluted by trivial agreement: instances where all $N$ samples produce identical (possibly incorrect) outputs receive EM${=}1$ regardless of quality, compressing the signal's dynamic range.
On the conditional set---where the model demonstrably produces varied outputs---exact agreement becomes the strongest quality signal.
The margin over SJ is largest on RE ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.171$), where compound extraction decisions amplify output variability, and smallest on CoNLL LLaMA ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.002$), where all signals converge near $\rho{\approx}0.46$.

\paragraph{WNUT-17 full signal analysis.}
Table~\ref{tab:wnut} (\S\ref{sec:qe_results}) reports all five signals on WNUT-17 with full-set and conditional $\rho$.
The full-set $p$-values are: VC ${<}$1e-112, FK $p{=}0.001$, SJ $p{=}0.020$, EM $p{=}0.194$, LP ${<}$1e-28.
VC's high full-set $\rho{=}0.724$ is entirely driven by the zero/non-zero boundary (conditional $\rho{=}0.038$, $p{=}0.49$), while LP's conditional $\rho{=}0.350$ is the highest among all signals on the non-zero subset, confirming that full-set correlations on high-failure-rate datasets conflate binary success prediction with quality gradation.

\paragraph{Cross-configuration selection analysis.}
Table~\ref{tab:cross_selection} extends the selection analysis to four additional configurations.
On LLaMA SciERC, where output diversity remains substantial (18\% identical outputs, 39\% unique), LP achieves the highest selection F1 (0.652) at $N{=}8$ but still falls within bootstrap noise of single-sample (0.646), replicating the gap observed on Qwen SciERC (Table~\ref{tab:selection}).
On CoNLL, 57--88\% of instances produce identical outputs across all $N$ samples, reflecting a ceiling effect (single-sample F1 ${\approx}$0.91--0.92) rather than signal failure; selection analysis on these configurations is uninformative because there is little per-sample variance for any signal to exploit.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection F1 (macro, instance-averaged) across configurations ($T{=}1.0$). Best non-oracle signal per row in \textbf{bold}. At $N{=}8$, no signal significantly outperforms greedy in any configuration. At $N{=}16$ on LLaMA CoNLL, VC achieves small but significant gains ($+0.28$~pp, $p{<}0.03$; see text below). CoNLL shows especially tight clustering where greedy already exceeds 0.90.}
\label{tab:cross_selection}
\begin{tabular}{llccccccc}
\toprule
Config & $n$ & Greedy & Oracle & SJ & FK & EM & LP & VC \\
\midrule
LLaMA/SciERC $N{=}8$ & 529 & .646 & .778 & .643 & .639 & .634 & \textbf{.652} & .633 \\
LLaMA/SciERC $N{=}16$ & 529 & .645 & .806 & \textbf{.649} & \textbf{.649} & .640 & .646 & .640 \\
Qwen/CoNLL $N{=}8$ & 2{,}756 & .908 & .948 & \textbf{.899} & .893 & .898 & .897 & .895 \\
LLaMA/CoNLL $N{=}8$ & 2{,}756 & .924 & .943 & .924 & \textbf{.925} & .924 & .924 & .923 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\paragraph{Diminishing returns of $N$-scaling.}
Our $N{=}8$ and $N{=}16$ comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:robustness}) characterize the marginal value of additional samples for test-time scaling \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2025scaling}.
For quality estimation, structural signals benefit consistently but sublinearly: SJ $\rho$ improves by $+0.047$ (Qwen SciERC, 3-seed mean) and $+0.032$ (LLaMA CoNLL, 3-seed mean) when doubling from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$, while log-probability is approximately $N$-invariant ($\Delta\rho{\leq}0.021$).
Structural signals leverage $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise comparisons (28 pairs at $N{=}8$, 120 at $N{=}16$), but the $\rho$ improvement is far less than proportional, indicating diminishing information per additional comparison.
This asymmetry gives structural signals a relative advantage in the compute-constrained regime: at $N{=}8$, SJ already achieves $\rho{=}0.431$ on LLaMA CoNLL (vs.\ LP $\rho{=}0.307$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.124$), and the gap \textit{widens} at $N{=}16$ ($\Delta{=}{+}0.163$) because structural signals continue to benefit from additional pairwise evidence while LP does not.
For sample selection, additional samples increase the oracle upper bound---more draws raise the probability of a high-quality candidate---but signal-based selection remains flat because the selector's inability to identify the best candidate is a granularity limitation, not a sample size limitation.
The practical implication is that $N{=}8$ captures most of the achievable quality estimation benefit; further scaling widens rather than closes the correlation-selection gap absent stronger per-sample selectors.

\paragraph{$N{=}16$ CoNLL selection: small but significant.}
While quality estimation benefits sublinearly from $N$-scaling, selection behavior at $N{=}16$ reveals a nuanced exception on LLaMA CoNLL.
VC achieves the largest gain over single-sample ($+0.28$~pp, $p{=}0.003$--$0.027$ across 3 seeds, all significant), with SJ, FK, and EM at $+0.22$--$0.23$~pp and LP at $+0.12$~pp (2/3 seeds significant).
These gains are statistically significant but practically minimal: oracle headroom at $N{=}16$ is only 2.5~pp, so VC captures approximately 10\% of the available headroom.
This reinforces the primary finding: even under the most favorable conditions---high baseline performance, more candidates, and aggregated multi-seed evidence---signal-based selection recovers only a fraction of the oracle headroom available.

\section{Bootstrap CI for Signal Comparisons}\label{app:bootstrap_signal}

Table~\ref{tab:bootstrap_signal_ci} reports bootstrap confidence intervals for individual signal $\rho$ and pairwise $\Delta\rho$ on SciERC NER ($N{=}8$, $n{=}529$, $B{=}10{,}000$, seed${=}42$).
The SJ--LP gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.155$) is clearly significant, confirming the structural advantage reported in \S\ref{sec:qe_results}.
The VC--SJ gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.019$) is not significant, indicating that these two structural signals perform comparably.
The SJ--EM gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.065$) is borderline significant, with the CI lower bound at $+0.003$ and upper bound at $+0.130$.

\centering
\small
\caption{Bootstrap 95\% CIs for signal $\rho$ on SciERC NER ($N{=}8$, $n{=}529$, $B{=}10{,}000$, seed${=}42$). Top: individual signals. Bottom: pairwise $\Delta\rho$; ``Sig.'' indicates whether the 95\% CI excludes zero.}
\label{tab:bootstrap_signal_ci}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Signal & $\rho$ & 95\% CI \\
\midrule
VC & +0.379 & [+0.299, +0.456] \\
SJ & +0.360 & [+0.277, +0.437] \\
EM & +0.295 & [+0.212, +0.371] \\
FK & +0.267 & [+0.176, +0.354] \\
LP & +0.205 & [+0.119, +0.291] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\vspace{0.5em}

\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
Comparison & $\Delta\rho$ & 95\% CI & Sig. \\
\midrule
SJ $-$ LP & +0.155 & [+0.074, +0.234] & Yes \\
VC $-$ SJ & +0.019 & [$-$0.033, +0.073] & No \\

\end{tabular}

\smallskip
{\footnotesize $^\dagger$Marginally significant without multiple comparison correction; would not survive Bonferroni correction for 10 pairwise comparisons ($\alpha_{\text{adj}}{=}0.005$).}
\end{table}

At $N{=}16$ ($B{=}10{,}000$, permutation test), the structural advantage extends to FK comparisons.
On SciERC NER ($n{=}529$), SJ--FK ($\Delta\rho{=}0.147$--$0.160$, all $p{\leq}0.002$) and VC--FK ($\Delta\rho{=}0.138$--$0.188$, all $p{\leq}0.003$) are clearly significant across all three seeds; EM--FK is seed-dependent ($\Delta\rho{=}0.054$--$0.093$, $p{=}0.048$--$0.15$).
On CoNLL ($n{=}2{,}756$), all signals significantly outperform FK: EM $\Delta\rho{=}0.071$ ($p{<}0.001$), SJ $\Delta\rho{=}0.056$ ($p{<}0.001$), VC $\Delta\rho{=}0.022$ ($p{=}0.040$).

\section{Diversity and Selection Analysis}\label{app:diversity}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_selection_gap}
\caption{The correlation-selection gap on SciERC NER ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$, 2-seed mean). Bars show best-of-$N$ selection F1; the line marks quality estimation $\rho$. Despite $\rho$ up to 0.40, no signal significantly outperforms single-sample (all $p{>}0.05$; Table~\ref{tab:selection}). Dashed line indicates oracle upper bound. RE selection results in Table~\ref{tab:selection}.}
\label{fig:selection_gap}
\end{figure*}

\paragraph{Output diversity quantification.}
Table~\ref{tab:diversity} summarizes output diversity across configurations.
On SciERC, output diversity is substantial: Qwen produces 43\% unique outputs per instance (mean 3.5 distinct out of $N{=}8$), with per-sample F1 standard deviation of 0.144 and mean pairwise SJ of 0.703.
LLaMA shows similar diversity (39\% unique, F1 std 0.11).
On CoNLL, diversity collapses: 57\% (Qwen) to 88\% (LLaMA) of instances produce identical outputs across all $N$ samples, reflecting a ceiling effect where single-sample F1 already exceeds 0.90.
WNUT-17 shows 55\% identical outputs, driven by the 52\% zero-F1 rate.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Output diversity across configurations ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). ``Identical'' = fraction of instances with all $N$ outputs identical. ``Unique'' = mean fraction of distinct outputs per instance.}
\label{tab:diversity}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Config & Identical & Unique \\
\midrule
Qwen/SciERC & 11\% & 43\% \\
LLaMA/SciERC & 18\% & 39\% \\
Qwen/CoNLL & 57\% & --- \\
LLaMA/CoNLL & 88\% & --- \\
WNUT-17 & 55\% & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Oracle-improvable fraction.}
Across SciERC configurations, 39--42\% of instances contain at least one sample with F1 exceeding single-sample\footnote{Oracle-improvable and diversity-stratified analyses use $n{=}529$ (excluding instances with empty gold annotations; see \S\ref{sec:evaluation}); the diversity quantification in Table~\ref{tab:diversity} uses the full test set.}: Qwen NER 42.0\% (222/529, mean headroom $+$31.9~pp among improvable instances), Qwen RE 41.3\% (164/397, $+$45.3~pp), LLaMA NER 39.3\% (208/529, $+$33.7~pp).
On CoNLL, only 4--9\% of instances are improvable, confirming the ceiling effect.

\paragraph{Diversity-stratified selection gap.}
On the 44\% of Qwen SciERC instances with high diversity (${\geq}4$ unique outputs among 8 samples, $n{=}232$), oracle headroom reaches $+$16.3~pp, yet all consistency-based signals (SJ, FK, EM, VC) select at or below single-sample, and LP---the only per-sample signal---achieves merely $+$0.8~pp.
LLaMA replicates this pattern: on its high-diversity subset ($n{=}186$), oracle headroom reaches $+$20.1~pp while consistency signals remain at or below single-sample and LP captures only $+$2.0~pp.
This rules out insufficient diversity as an explanation for the correlation-selection gap.

\paragraph{TOST equivalence testing.}\label{app:tost}
The primary evidence against selection gains comes from effect sizes and confidence intervals: Cohen's $d{=}0.038$ for the best signal (NER LP) and bootstrap 95\% CI [$-$3.0, $+$4.2]~pp spanning zero.
Table~\ref{tab:tost} supplements this with two one-sided tests (TOST), testing whether each signal's selection F1 is equivalent to single-sample within a bound $\delta$.
The $\delta$ values are contextualized against oracle headroom (12--18~pp): $\delta{=}5$~pp corresponds to forgoing 28--38\% of the available headroom, $\delta{=}3$~pp forgoing 17--23\%, and $\delta{=}2$~pp less than 15\%.
These proportions use the same test data that defines the headroom, introducing circularity: $\delta$ is anchored to the very quantity it contextualizes.
We address this below with externally anchored equivalence margins.
The breakpoint $\delta^*$---the minimum equivalence margin at which each signal passes TOST---ranges from approximately 1.3~pp (SJ, ${\sim}$10\% of oracle headroom) to 3.4~pp (FK, ${\sim}$26\%) on NER, and from approximately 2.9~pp (LP, ${\sim}$16\%) to 6.5~pp (VC, ${\sim}$36\%) on RE.
On NER ($n{=}529$), at $\delta{=}{\pm}2$~pp, SJ and LP are confirmed equivalent to single-sample (TOST $p{<}0.05$); at $\delta{=}{\pm}3$~pp, four of five signals pass; at $\delta{=}{\pm}5$~pp, all five pass.
On RE ($n{=}397$, preliminary), EM and VC fail equivalence even at $\delta{=}{\pm}5$~pp due to systematic underperformance ($\Delta{=}{-}3.2$~pp and $-4.5$~pp respectively).
The effect sizes are negligible ($d{=}0.038$) and confidence intervals span zero, with TOST confirming equivalence at practically meaningful margins.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{TOST equivalence testing: signals vs.\ single-sample on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). \checkmark: equivalent at $p{<}0.05$; \texttimes: not equivalent. $\Delta$: mean F1 difference (signal $-$ single-sample).}
\label{tab:tost}
\begin{tabular}{l cccc cccc}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{NER}} & \multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{RE}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-5} \cmidrule(lr){6-9}
Signal & $\Delta$ & $\pm$2 & $\pm$3 & $\pm$5 & $\Delta$ & $\pm$2 & $\pm$3 & $\pm$5 \\
\midrule
LP & +0.6 & \checkmark & \checkmark & \checkmark & $-$0.9 & \texttimes & \checkmark & \checkmark \\
SJ & +0.1 & \checkmark & \checkmark & \checkmark & $-$1.8 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \checkmark \\
FK & $-$0.5 & \texttimes & \checkmark & \checkmark & $-$1.6 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \checkmark \\
EM & $-$0.8 & \texttimes & \checkmark & \checkmark & $-$3.2 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \texttimes \\
VC & $-$1.0 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \checkmark & $-$4.5 & \texttimes & \texttimes & \texttimes \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{External equivalence margins.}
The oracle-headroom anchors above introduce circularity, as a reviewer correctly noted: $\delta$ is calibrated against the very quantity it contextualizes.
To resolve this, we supplement with three externally grounded margins:
(1) $\delta_{\mathrm{SEM}}$: the bootstrapped standard error of single-sample F1 (0.43--1.33~pp depending on configuration), representing measurement noise;
(2) $\delta_{\mathrm{practical}}{=}0.5$~pp, reflecting the threshold below which NER differences are considered negligible \cite{ratinov2009design};
(3) $\delta_{\mathrm{literature}}{=}1.0$~pp, the approximate significant-difference threshold established in NER evaluation methodology \cite{bergkirkpatrick2012empirical}.

Results under these external anchors diverge sharply by configuration.
On LLaMA CoNLL ($n{=}2{,}756$), all signals pass equivalence at every $\delta$ ($p{<}0.001$), consistent with the near-zero selection deltas ($|\Delta|{\leq}0.1$~pp) and tight CIs at this sample size.
On Qwen CoNLL ($n{=}2{,}756$), no signal passes at any external $\delta$: selection F1 degrades by 0.9--1.5~pp relative to single-sample, exceeding even $\delta_{\mathrm{literature}}$.
On SciERC NER ($n{=}529$), only SJ passes at $\delta_{\mathrm{SEM}}{=}1.33$~pp (the widest SEM bound); all other signals and tighter margins fail.
These external anchors confirm that the equivalence conclusion is configuration-dependent: LLaMA CoNLL selection is robustly equivalent to single-sample under any reasonable margin, while SciERC and Qwen CoNLL selection shows detectable degradation at externally calibrated thresholds.

\paragraph{Multiple comparison considerations.}\label{app:multiple_comparisons}
Our primary selection analysis involves ${\sim}$20 comparisons (5 signals $\times$ 3--4 configurations).
Since all primary selection results are non-significant ($p{>}0.05$), applying Benjamini-Hochberg correction can only make these results more conservative, strengthening the ``no signal beats greedy'' conclusion.
The sole positive finding---non-tied LP subset ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.004$; \S\ref{sec:discussion})---survives Bonferroni correction over 5 signal comparisons ($p_{\mathrm{adj}}{=}0.020 < 0.05$), as noted in the main text footnote.
For quality estimation signal rankings, differences between the top signals (e.g., VC vs.\ SJ on SciERC) should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as statistically confirmed orderings, given the limited power of 3-seed comparisons.

\section{Multi-Seed Stability}\label{app:multiseed}

Table~\ref{tab:multiseed} reports quality estimation metrics across three random seeds for both model families on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$).
On NER, the signal ranking VC${>}$SJ${>}$EM${>}$FK${>}$LP is identical across all six model-seed combinations, with $\sigma{\leq}0.025$ for all signals (rankings are stable across our 3 seeds, though statistical power with $n{=}3$ is limited).
On RE (Qwen only, preliminary), VC remains the top signal ($\rho{=}0.309{\pm}0.024$), but LP rises to \#2 ($\rho{=}0.297{\pm}0.022$), above FK, SJ, and EM---a reversal from the NER ranking that reflects RE's higher sensitivity to per-sample scoring.
LLaMA absolute values are systematically lower than Qwen on NER, consistent with the directionally-consistent-but-magnitude-dependent characterization in the main text.

\label{tab:multiseed}

449	\paragraph{Prompt template.}
450	For NER, we use a structured prompt:
451	\begin{quote}
452	\small
453	\texttt{System:} You are an expert in Named Entity Recognition.\\
454	\texttt{User:} Extract all named entities from the following text. Output as JSON.\\
455	Text: \texttt{\{input\_text\}}\\
456	Entity types: \texttt{\{schema\_types\}}
457	\end{quote}
458	RE follows the same structure with ``Relation Extraction'' and relation type lists substituted accordingly.
459	
460	\paragraph{Constrained decoding.}
461	Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar-based JSON schema enforcement \cite{willard2023guided}, which constrains outputs to valid entity/relation structures matching the target schema.
462	This eliminates format errors but may compress per-sample diversity by restricting the output space.\footnote{SciERC training used \texttt{enable\_thinking=True} (LLaMA Factory 0.9.4 default), injecting empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks (4--5 tokens) into each training response with loss computation; CoNLL and WNUT explicitly set \texttt{enable\_thinking=False}. Constrained decoding at inference time enforces JSON-only output, suppressing thinking tokens. See \S\ref{sec:setup} and Limitations for discussion of this confound.}
463	
464	\section{Thinking Token Impact Analysis}\label{app:thinking_token}
465	
466	Qwen3-8B's SciERC checkpoint was trained with empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks prepended to each response (\S\ref{sec:setup}).
467	We quantify the potential impact on LP scores through three complementary arguments.
468	
469	\paragraph{LP shift magnitude.}
470	Empty thinking tokens (mean 4.5 per sample) constitute 2.1\% of tokens on SciERC.
471	The estimated LP shift is 0.001 nats per token (2.68\% of the median within-instance LP range of 0.041 nats).
472	Because all samples share identical thinking-token LP offsets, cumulative LP rankings are invariant; mean LP changes selection for ${<}1.5\%$ of instances.
473	
474	\paragraph{Constant prefix cancellation.}
475	All $N$ samples within an instance share the same prompt and, under constrained decoding, the same absence of thinking tokens at inference time.
476	Any LP bias from the training-time thinking prefix is therefore a near-constant additive shift across all candidates within an instance, leaving within-instance LP \textit{rankings} unchanged.
477	
478	\paragraph{CoNLL control group.}
479	CoNLL and WNUT-17 checkpoints were trained without thinking tokens (\texttt{enable\_thinking=False}).
480	If thinking tokens caused LP compression on SciERC, CoNLL should exhibit lower tied fractions.
481	Instead, CoNLL shows \textit{higher} tied fractions at both temperatures (86.8\% at $T{=}1.0$, 95.8\% at $T{=}0.7$) than SciERC (60.3\% at $T{=}1.0$), directly contradicting the thinking-token hypothesis.
482	
483	\section{Log-Probability Score Compression}\label{app:logprob_ties}
484	
485	Under constrained decoding, log-probability scores are severely compressed within instances, limiting per-sample discrimination (Table~\ref{tab:logprob_ties}, Figure~\ref{fig:lp_range_cdf}).
486	The median within-instance LP range is only 0.041 nats; we use $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ as an illustrative threshold to characterize this compression.
487	At this cutpoint, 60.3\% of instances ($n{=}529$, excluding empty gold annotations) have a within-sample range below $\varepsilon$, and 75\% of pairwise comparisons are effective ties ($|\Delta|{<}0.026$).
488	The CDF rises smoothly with no cliff or discontinuity (Figure~\ref{fig:lp_range_cdf}), confirming that compression is a pervasive regime rather than a bimodal split.
489	This compression is stable across seeds: seed${=}456$ yields median LP range${=}0.040$ nats and tied fraction${=}62.2\%$ (vs.\ seed${=}42$: $0.041$ nats, $60.3\%$).
490	Seed~456 uses a different subtask flag (joint vs.\ ner for seeds 42 and 123); the LP distributions are statistically indistinguishable (median LP: 8.37 vs.\ 8.20 nats; Mann--Whitney $p{=}0.55$), confirming that the subtask change does not affect compression.
491	For comparison, SJ has only 12.5\% tied instances at the same threshold---SJ's advantage over LP for selection is one of score resolution, not information content.
492	
493	\begin{figure}[t]
494	\centering
495	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig_lp_range_cdf}
496	\caption{CDF of within-instance LP range on SciERC NER ($N{=}8$, $n{=}529$). The median LP range is 0.041 nats (dashed line), below $\varepsilon{=}0.05$. The smooth CDF confirms compression is pervasive, not bimodal.}
497	\label{fig:lp_range_cdf}
498	\end{figure}
499	
500	\begin{table}[t]
501	\centering
502	\small
503	\caption{Log-probability score compression on SciERC NER ($N{=}8$, $n{=}529$). ``Tied'' = fraction of instances where within-instance LP range ${<}\varepsilon$.}
504	\label{tab:logprob_ties}
505	\begin{tabular}{lc}
506	\toprule
507	$\varepsilon$ threshold & Tied instances (\%) \\
508	\midrule
509	0.01 & 1.1\% \\
510	0.05 & 60.3\% \\
511	0.1  & ${\sim}$84\% \\
512	0.5  & ${\sim}$99\% \\
513	\bottomrule
514	\end{tabular}
515	\end{table}

691	\section{MBR Decoding and Task-Specific Interactions}\label{app:mbr_discussion}
692	
693	\paragraph{Connection to MBR decoding.}
694	Our selection strategies instantiate minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, muller2021understanding}: each selects $\hat{y} = \arg\max_{y_i} \sum_{j \neq i} U(y_i, y_j)$ with utility $U$ defined by SJ, EM, or entity overlap.
695	Despite MBR's success in machine translation \cite{freitag2022high} and its extension to summarization, code generation, and captioning \cite{jinnai2024mbr}, all variants fail here: despite positive within-instance utility--F1 correlation, selection gains are limited by instance degeneracy---the core of the correlation-selection gap.
696	\citet{eikema2025structured} study structure-conditional MBR decoding and find that standard utility functions degrade on structured outputs---consistent with our finding that consensus-proximity selection fails in IE despite its success in machine translation.

\paragraph{Prompt template.}
For NER, we use a structured prompt:
\begin{quote}
\small
\texttt{System:} You are an expert in Named Entity Recognition.\\
\texttt{User:} Extract all named entities from the following text. Output as JSON.\\
Text: \texttt{\{input\_text\}}\\
Entity types: \texttt{\{schema\_types\}}
\end{quote}
RE follows the same structure with ``Relation Extraction'' and relation type lists substituted accordingly.

\paragraph{Constrained decoding.}
Inference uses vLLM with XGrammar-based JSON schema enforcement \cite{willard2023guided}, which constrains outputs to valid entity/relation structures matching the target schema.
This eliminates format errors but may compress per-sample diversity by restricting the output space.\footnote{SciERC training used \texttt{enable\_thinking=True} (LLaMA Factory 0.9.4 default), injecting empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks (4--5 tokens) into each training response with loss computation; CoNLL and WNUT explicitly set \texttt{enable\_thinking=False}. Constrained decoding at inference time enforces JSON-only output, suppressing thinking tokens. See \S\ref{sec:setup} and Limitations for discussion of this confound.}

\section{Thinking Token Impact Analysis}\label{app:thinking_token}

Qwen3-8B's SciERC checkpoint was trained with empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks prepended to each response (\S\ref{sec:setup}).
We quantify the potential impact on LP scores through three complementary arguments.

\paragraph{LP shift magnitude.}
Empty thinking tokens (mean 4.5 per sample) constitute 2.1\% of tokens on SciERC.
The estimated LP shift is 0.001 nats per token (2.68\% of the median within-instance LP range of 0.041 nats).
Because all samples share identical thinking-token LP offsets, cumulative LP rankings are invariant; mean LP changes selection for ${<}1.5\%$ of instances.

\paragraph{Constant prefix cancellation.}
All $N$ samples within an instance share the same prompt and, under constrained decoding, the same absence of thinking tokens at inference time.
Any LP bias from the training-time thinking prefix is therefore a near-constant additive shift across all candidates within an instance, leaving within-instance LP \textit{rankings} unchanged.

\paragraph{CoNLL control group.}
CoNLL and WNUT-17 checkpoints were trained without thinking tokens (\texttt{enable\_thinking=False}).
If thinking tokens caused LP compression on SciERC, CoNLL should exhibit lower tied fractions.
Instead, CoNLL shows \textit{higher} tied fractions at both temperatures (86.8\% at $T{=}1.0$, 95.8\% at $T{=}0.7$) than SciERC (60.3\% at $T{=}1.0$), directly contradicting the thinking-token hypothesis.

\section{Log-Probability Score Compression}\label{app:logprob_ties}

Under constrained decoding, log-probability scores are severely compressed within instances, limiting per-sample discrimination (Table~\ref{tab:logprob_ties}, Figure~\ref{fig:lp_range_cdf}).
The median within-instance LP range is only 0.041 nats; we use $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ as an illustrative threshold to characterize this compression.
At this cutpoint, 60.3\% of instances ($n{=}529$, excluding empty gold annotations) have a within-sample range below $\varepsilon$, and 75\% of pairwise comparisons are effective ties ($|\Delta|{<}0.026$).
The CDF rises smoothly with no cliff or discontinuity (Figure~\ref{fig:lp_range_cdf}), confirming that compression is a pervasive regime rather than a bimodal split.
This compression is stable across seeds: seed${=}456$ yields median LP range${=}0.040$ nats and tied fraction${=}62.2\%$ (vs.\ seed${=}42$: $0.041$ nats, $60.3\%$).
Seed~456 uses a different subtask flag (joint vs.\ ner for seeds 42 and 123); the LP distributions are statistically indistinguishable (median LP: 8.37 vs.\ 8.20 nats; Mann--Whitney $p{=}0.55$), confirming that the subtask change does not affect compression.
For comparison, SJ has only 12.5\% tied instances at the same threshold---SJ's advantage over LP for selection is one of score resolution, not information content.

RE miscalibration is more severe than NER (ECE 0.109--0.339; Figure~\ref{fig:reliability}).

\paragraph{Selection.}
Table~\ref{tab:re_cond_selection} presents RE selection at $N{=}8$: no signal outperforms single-sample (0.404) on the full set ($n{=}397$) or the non-zero subset ($n{=}238$), with 18.1~pp of unrealized oracle headroom.
At $N{=}16$ (Qwen3-4B, Table~\ref{tab:re_n16_selection}), LP is the sole positive signal ($\Delta{=}{+}0.7$~pp, $p{=}0.058$), consistent with LP being the strongest RE selection signal across scales.

\paragraph{Scale ablation.}
At 4B scale (Qwen3-4B, $N{=}8$, $\text{seed}{=}42$), RE quality estimation shows FK $\rho{=}0.359$ and LP $\rho{=}0.351$, both above their 8B counterparts (FK 0.275, LP 0.266), while SJ declines ($0.267$ vs.\ $0.250$).
Selection remains below single-sample on RE ($\Delta$ up to $-3.4$~pp) despite 17.1~pp of oracle headroom.

\paragraph{Free-form decoding.}
RE LP selection consistently reverses direction under free-form decoding ($+1.8{\pm}0.1$~pp across 4 seeds vs.\ $-0.9$~pp under constrained decoding at 8B; \S\ref{app:freeform_ablation}), suggesting constrained decoding's fixed template obscures LP signal in RE (\S\ref{app:mbr_discussion}).

\section{RE Conditional Selection}\label{app:re_conditional_selection}

Table~\ref{tab:re_cond_selection} extends the selection analysis to the RE non-zero F1 subset.
Of $n{=}397$ RE instances, 238 (60\%) have non-zero F1 and 159 (40\%) have zero F1.
All five signals underperform single-sample on both subsets.
On the non-zero subset, selection performance is \textit{worse} than on the full set (e.g., VC: $-10.0$~pp on non-zero vs.\ $-4.5$~pp on full set), because single-sample is already strong on non-zero instances (F1${=}0.674$) and signals actively select inferior samples.
Oracle headroom exists (0.757 vs.\ 0.674) but no signal exploits it, ruling out the 40\% zero-F1 floor effect as the explanation for RE selection failure.

\section{RE $N{=}16$ Selection Analysis}\label{app:re_n16_selection}

Table~\ref{tab:re_n16_selection} extends the selection analysis to RE at $N{=}16$ with 3-seed statistics.
All four consistency signals underperform single-sample, with EM showing the largest deficit ($\Delta{=}{-}1.5$~pp, Fisher $p{>}0.99$).
LP is the only positive signal ($\Delta{=}{+}0.7$~pp, Fisher $p{=}0.058$), driven primarily by seed~456 ($\Delta{=}{+}1.5$~pp, $p{=}0.026$); the remaining seeds show smaller effects ($+0.1$ and $+0.6$~pp, $p{>}0.20$).
Even the most favorable seed captures only ${\sim}9\%$ of the 17.1~pp oracle headroom.
This cross-task consistency---LP as the only viable selection signal on both NER and RE---reinforces the persistent limitation of instance-level signals for candidate ranking across tested regimes.

\section{MBR Decoding and Task-Specific Interactions}\label{app:mbr_discussion}

\paragraph{Connection to MBR decoding.}
Our selection strategies instantiate minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, muller2021understanding}: each selects $\hat{y} = \arg\max_{y_i} \sum_{j \neq i} U(y_i, y_j)$ with utility $U$ defined by SJ, EM, or entity overlap.
Despite MBR's success in machine translation \cite{freitag2022high} and its extension to summarization, code generation, and captioning \cite{jinnai2024mbr}, all variants fail here: despite positive within-instance utility--F1 correlation, selection gains are limited by instance degeneracy---the core of the correlation-selection gap.
\citet{eikema2025structured} study structure-conditional MBR decoding and find that standard utility functions degrade on structured outputs---consistent with our finding that consensus-proximity selection fails in IE despite its success in machine translation.

\paragraph{Task-specific decoding interactions.}

698	\paragraph{Task-specific decoding interactions.}
699	The free-form ablation reveals divergent behavior across tasks.
700	On RE, LP selection flips from $-0.68$~pp (constrained) to $+1.69$~pp (free-form; preliminary, single RE benchmark), a reversal that spans all 7 relation types and is driven by selective variance reallocation ($p{<}0.0001$).
701	The win/loss ratio shifts from 36:59 (constrained) to 45:45 (free-form), with the gains concentrated on relation-dense instances (mean 3.3 gold relations).
702	This interaction does not generalize to NER, where selection remains negligible under both regimes.
703	This ablation uses a single seed (seed${=}42$); whether the RE reversal replicates across seeds and generalizes to other RE benchmarks warrants further investigation.
704	The non-tied subset ($n{=}210$) is partially reshuffled under free-form decoding: Jaccard similarity between the constrained and free-form non-tied sets is 0.472, indicating that 87 instances newly gain LP discrimination while others lose it, yielding a $3{\times}$ increase in within-instance LP range for the newly non-tied subset.
705	Despite this reshuffling, aggregate NER selection gains remain negligible---score compression is not a fixed property of specific instances but rather a pervasive regime that shifts across instances without producing net selection improvement.
706	Free-form decoding also slightly improves quality estimation (NER VC $\rho$: 0.379$\to$0.409), though this does not translate to selection gains.

793	\paragraph{CoNLL NER free-form results.}
794	Extending the free-form ablation to CoNLL NER (Qwen3-8B, 4 seeds, $N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$), LP range median is $0.058{\pm}0.007$ across seeds---higher than SciERC ($0.041$) but still compressed given CoNLL's 86.8\% tied fraction under constrained decoding.

803	\paragraph{Pairwise overlap.}

806	
807	\paragraph{Instance complexity drives failure.}
808	Table~\ref{tab:stable_failures} stratifies instances by failure stability.
809	Stable failures (all 3 seeds) involve more gold relations (2.12 vs.\ 1.62 for never-fail instances) and higher single-sample F1 (0.688 vs.\ 0.429), indicating that LP mis-selects on instances where the model already performs well---precisely the instances where selection would be most valuable.

VerbConf achieves higher $\rho$ than LP on both datasets (SciERC: 0.297 vs.\ 0.205; CoNLL: 0.337 vs.\ 0.316) and competitive AUROC (SciERC: 0.681 vs.\ 0.578; CoNLL: 0.747 vs.\ 0.753), yet yields the worst selection among all signals ($\Delta{=}{-}2.45$~pp on SciERC, $-1.93$~pp on CoNLL).
This dissociation further demonstrates the correlation-selection gap: a signal can rank instances by expected quality without being able to discriminate candidates within an instance.
The AUROC--$\rho$ decoupling on CoNLL (LP leads AUROC at 0.753 while VerbConf leads $\rho$ at 0.337) reflects differing sensitivity to binary vs.\ ordinal discrimination.

\section{LLaMA-3.2-3B Scale Ablation}\label{app:llama3b}

To extend scale coverage below 4B, we fine-tune LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct on SciERC NER under identical training conditions (LoRA rank${=}32$, $\alpha{=}64$, 5 epochs) and evaluate quality estimation and selection (Table~\ref{tab:llama3b}).

\label{tab:llama3b}
\begin{tabular}{l cc cc}

Signal & $\rho$ & AUROC & Sel.\ F1 & $\Delta$ vs.\ greedy \\
\midrule

The $\rho$ ranking at 3B (VC $>$ SJ $>$ EM $>$ FK $\approx$ LP) preserves the structural-over-LP ordering from 8B (Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}), confirming ranking stability across two model families spanning 3B--8B.
AUROC rankings differ (EM $>$ VC $>$ SJ $>$ FK $>$ LP), reflecting the $\rho$--AUROC dissociation noted in the main text.
Despite 13.63~pp of oracle headroom, no signal achieves significant selection improvement (best: SJ, $+0.61$~pp, $p{=}0.175$); VC---the strongest QE signal---yields the worst selection ($-1.54$~pp), consistent with the correlation-selection gap observed at larger scales.

\section{Few-NERD Full Results}\label{app:fewnerd}

Table~\ref{tab:fewnerd_full} reports the complete Few-NERD INTRA coarse evaluation (Qwen3-8B, LoRA rank${=}32$, 3 epochs, $N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$).
After gold-filtering (removing instances with no gold entities), the evaluation set contains $n{=}32{,}565$ instances across 8 coarse entity types; 11.9\% receive zero F1 under greedy decoding.
Instance degeneracy is 10.1\% (vs.\ 21\% on SciERC, 58\% on CoNLL).

- Soundness (1-5)
- Excitement (1-5)

Let me write a thorough review focused on method rigor and experimental design as instructed.


The paper demonstrates strong experimental rigor with comprehensive testing across multiple datasets, model sizes, and random seeds, supported by solid statistical methods including bootstrap confidence intervals and equivalence testing. The core contribution—the correlation-selection gap and its three-layer diagnostic framework—is well-articulated and systematically validated, with honest acknowledgment of limitations like the low seed count. The authors present negative results carefully with appropriate caveats, and their degeneracy analysis provides genuine insight into the phenomenon.

On methodological grounds, the soft Jaccard denominator choice is well-justified by the data, the instance-level versus per-sample distinction is cleanly formalized, and the MBR/consensus-proximity equivalence is properly established. The reported within-instance correlation of ρ = 0.52 for MBR utility is compelling, though showing the full distribution rather than just the median would be more convincing. The primary analysis relies on a single seed, which they acknowledge, but the three-seed stability check with σ ≤ 0.026 provides reasonable reassurance about ranking consistency.

However, the correlation-selection gap phenomenon is demonstrated on only three datasets with a monotonic degeneracy gradient, which is a limited sample size for making cross-dataset claims—though the entity-type analysis within Few-NERD does expand this to eight cases. The LoRA rank ablation is more problematic: at rank 8, degeneracy drops to 7.2% with 16 percentage points of headroom, yet selection still fails. The paper argues this shows degeneracy is necessary but not sufficient, but the ablation actually conflates two variables—low degeneracy and LP compression both change together. To properly support the "not sufficient" claim, they'd need to show a case where degeneracy is low and LP compression isn't present, yet selection still fails. The Few-NERD results actually point in the opposite direction, suggesting that when degeneracy is genuinely low, the dynamics shift.

The free-form decoding ablation further complicates the "model-intrinsic compression" narrative: on NER it holds (std ratio 0.97), but on RE, free-form decoding recovers selection performance by 2.35 percentage points, indicating the phenomenon is task-dependent rather than universally intrinsic to the model. The non-tied subset analysis with ε=0.05 relies on post-hoc threshold selection, though the monotonic trends and Bonferroni correction provide some rigor despite the data-snooping concerns the authors acknowledge. The oracle headroom calculation using max F1 across samples is standard and unproblematic, while the sign test at n=529 across two seeds forms the core of the selection stability assessment.

However, there's a missing power analysis—with p=0.29 and effect size d=0.038, I need to determine what power this test actually has to detect a 1 percentage point improvement, which is crucial for interpreting the negative result. Additionally, Few-NERD uses only 3 training epochs versus 5 for SciERC, which could confound the degeneracy comparison between datasets. The evaluation protocols also vary across datasets (gold-filtered versus full-set, different N values) without always being transparent about these differences in the main text.

I'm working through several specific concerns: the "necessary but not sufficient" claim about LoRA rank=8 conflates two simultaneous changes—degeneracy drops while model quality also degrades from lower rank. The cross-dataset degeneracy gradient relies on just 3 datasets, which is too limited for the causal claims being made, though the entity-type analysis within Few-NERD (n=8) is more granular but still confounds entity difficulty with degeneracy. There's also an internal contradiction where the free-form decoding conclusion that "compression is model-intrinsic" conflicts with the RE results showing free-form actually does recover selection. Now I need to structure these critiques into a coherent review.

The statistical power issue is significant here—the paper doesn't report power analyses, and for the main SciERC selection result with such a small effect size and sample, the ability to detect even a 1 percentage point effect is probably insufficient. This is particularly problematic since the paper's core argument hinges on a negative result.

# Round 1 Review — Reviewer 1 (方法严谨性 + 实验设计)

**Paper**: "Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: Why Confidence Signals Fail to Scale Structured Information Extraction"

---

## Summary (2-3 句)

本文系统评估了 5 种 confidence signals 在 LLM-based NER 中的 quality estimation 和 sample selection 能力，发现 QE 成功但 selection 失败（correlation-selection gap），并通过 instance degeneracy 和 LP compression 两个机制给出诊断。实验设计严谨度高于平均水准（多数据集、多模型、多 seed、bootstrap/TOST 统计检验），但部分核心 claim 的因果推断证据不足，跨数据集梯度 n=3 支撑的泛化结论需要审慎对待。

---

## Strengths

1. **问题定义清晰且有贡献** (Section 1, 3.3): "correlation-selection gap" 的概念化有价值——将 QE 和 selection 明确解耦，指出一个被 prior work 忽略的 confound。instance-level vs per-sample 的形式化区分（Section 3.1）简洁且数��上正确。

2. **实验设计的系统性** (Section 4): 4 个 NER benchmark 构成 difficulty gradient（WNUT-17 collapse → SciERC medium → Few-NERD low-degeneracy → CoNLL ceiling），每个数据集的角色清晰。两个模型族（Qwen3-8B, LLaMA-3.1-8B）加 4B/3B ablation 排除模型特异性。

3. **统计方法论上佳** (Section 4.3, Appendix): Bootstrap CI（B=10,000）、paired sign test、TOST 等效性检验、Bonferroni 校正、Kendall's W 排名稳定性、Fisher 合并 p 值——统计工具选择恰当，且在负面结果中使用 TOST 避免了"absence of evidence = evidence of absence"的谬误。

4. **三层诊断结构有说服力** (Section 4.3): (a) instance-level 信号 by construction 不能排名候选 → (b) MBR with aligned utility 因 degeneracy 失败 → (c) LP 有 per-sample 信息但被 compression 限制。逻辑递进清晰。

5. **负面结果的审慎表达**: 论文多处使用"inversely associated with"而非"causes"，使用"necessary but not sufficient"限定 claim，Limitations 节详尽列举未覆盖条件。

6. **Appendix 丰富且组织有序**: 涵盖 FK independence test、SJ normalizer robustness、ε robustness、thinking token impact、OOD analysis 等，大多数潜在反驳都有对应的 ablation 或 control。

---

## Weaknesses

### [Must-Fix] W1: 跨数据集 degeneracy 梯度的因果推断基础薄弱 (n=3)

- **位置**: Section 4.4 (Table 4), Section 5 "Regime boundaries", Figure 3
- **问题**: 论文的核心 claim 之一是 "LP selection effectiveness is inversely associated with degeneracy rate across datasets"，但这一梯度仅基于 n=3 数据集（CoNLL 58% → SciERC 21% → Few-NERD 10%）。任何三个数据点的单调排列概率为 1/3!= 1/6，即使在随机条件下也有 16.7% 的概率出现单调趋势。
- **补充**: 论文试图用 entity-type-level analysis（n=8, ρ=-0.881, p=0.004）加强论证，但 entity type 之间共享同一模型、同一 checkpoint、同一 inference pipeline，违反独立性假设。不同 entity type 的 degeneracy 差异可能源自 type frequency、schema complexity 等混淆变量，而非 degeneracy 本身直接导致 LP selection 差异。
- **Figure 3 的 pooled correlation (ρ=-0.57, p=0.066, n=11) 混合了两个粒度的观测**，统计上有问题：cross-dataset aggregates 和 per-entity-type points 的方差结构完全不同，不应直接 pool。
- **为什么影响接收**: 如果 degeneracy 梯度的因果解释不成立，Contribution 3 的基础动摇。
- **建议**: (a) 增加至少 2-3 个数据集的实验（如 OntoNotes、ACE05）扩大 n；(b) 用 Few-NERD 内 entity-type analysis 时，控制 type frequency 和 entity boundary difficulty 等混淆变量；(c) 不要 pool 不同粒度的观测到同一 correlation。

### [Must-Fix] W2: "Necessary but not sufficient" claim 的 LoRA-rank ablation 存在混淆变量

- **位置**: Section 4.5 "LoRA-rank ablation" (line: "Low degeneracy is thus a necessary but not sufficient condition for selection")
- **问题**: LoRA rank=8 ablation 降低了 degeneracy (21% → 7.2%) 且增加了 oracle headroom (13.3 → 16.0 pp)，但 LP selection 仍失败。论文据此声称 degeneracy 是 "necessary but not sufficient"。但 LoRA rank=8 同时降低了模型能力（greedy F1: 0.645 → 0.640），改变了学到的 representation space。LP compression 在 rank=8 下可能因模型能力下降而加剧，而非因为 degeneracy 本身不充分。
- **矛盾**: Few-NERD 在 10% degeneracy 下 LP selection 成功 (+1.36 pp)，而 rank=8 SciERC 在 7.2% degeneracy 下仍失败。如果 degeneracy 是唯一 gating factor，Few-NERD 的成功和 rank=8 SciERC 的失败之间的差异需要更好的解释。论文在 Section 4.4 简要提到 "LP signal quality (ρ) provides an additional prerequisite"，但这实质上是在说 degeneracy + LP quality 联���决定 selection，而非 degeneracy alone is necessary。
- **为什么影响接收**: "Necessary but not sufficient" 是一个精确的逻辑声明；当前实验设计无法将 degeneracy 从 LP compression 中独立隔离。
- **建议**: (a) 明确指出 LoRA rank ablation 同时改变了多个变量（degeneracy、model quality、LP compression degree），不能做 clean causal attribution；(b) 将 claim 弱化为 "low degeneracy co-occurs with LP selection success, but rank-8 ablation shows it is not alone sufficient"；(c) 最好提供 rank=8 下的 LP compression 统计（median LP range、tied fraction），以量化 compression 在两种 rank 下的变化。

### [Should-Fix] W3: 负面结果的统计功效 (power) 未报告

- **位置**: Section 4.3 (Table 3, "LP achieves only 0.647, Δ=+0.2 pp, d=0.038, p=0.29")
- **问题**: 论文的中心论点是负面结果（selection 不显著优于 greedy）。对于负面结果，需要报告 power analysis：在当前样本量 (n=529) 和 seed 数量 (2) 下，检测 1 pp 效应（一个实际有意义的改进）的统计功效是多少？如果 power 很低（如 <50%），则 p=0.29 无法区分 "真的没效果" 和 "效果存在但检测不到"。
- **TOST 部分缓解了这个问题** (Appendix D)，但 TOST 使用的 δ=2pp (internal anchor) 是否过宽？externally anchored δ=1.0pp 下，SciERC 未通过 TOST。
- **为什么影响评分**: 虽然 TOST 是好的补充，但主文没有明确讨论 power，可能误导读者认为 "p>0.05" 等同于 "确认无效果"。
- **建议**: 在 main text 或 appendix 中加入 post-hoc power analysis，报告当前设计检测 Δ=1pp 的 power；或者明确指出 Few-NERD (n=32,565) 的结果 (LP +1.36 pp, p<0.001) 才是 definitive evidence，SciERC 的 non-significance 可能受限于 power。

### [Should-Fix] W4: "Compression is model-intrinsic" 的结论与 RE 结果矛盾

- **位置**: Section 5 "Ablation: free-form decoding" + Appendix H (Table 8)
- **问题**: 论文 NER free-form ablation 发现 LP 分布几乎不变 (std ratio 0.97)，据此声称 "compression is model-intrinsic rather than constraint-imposed"。但 RE 的 free-form decoding 显著恢复了 LP selection (+2.35 pp, p=0.025)，直接证明 constraints DO compress LP for RE。
- **论文在 Section 5 最后简要提到这一分歧**，但 Abstract 和 Introduction 中 "compression is model-intrinsic" 的 framing 没有 qualification。读者如果只看主文可能误以为这是普适结论。
- **为什么影响评分**: 论文的诊断框架混淆了 task-specific behavior 和 universal mechanism。
- **建议**: (a) 将主文 claim 限定为 "for NER, compression is model-intrinsic; for RE, constraint-imposed mechanisms contribute significantly"；(b) 在 Abstract 或 Introduction 的 diagnostic chain 描述中加入 task qualifier。

### [Should-Fix] W5: Primary seed (seed=42) 的代表性与 selection 实验的 2-seed 限制

- **位置**: Section 4.1 footnote 4 ("Quality estimation uses a single primary seed; selection uses 2-seed averages")
- **问题**: QE 主结果仅 1 seed，selection 仅 2 seeds。虽然 Table 6 的 3-seed stability test 显示 σ≤0.026 for ρ rankings，但 selection F1 的 seed variance 未被同样充分量化。Table 3 报告的 selection F1 σ（如 LP: ±0.005）基于仅 2 seeds 的极差，这不是可靠的 variance estimate。
- **Few-NERD 是 1-seed result** (Table 4)，尽管 n=32,565 提供了足够 statistical power，但 systematic bias（如训练 seed 影响 degeneracy rate）仍可能存在。
- **建议**: 至少为 Few-NERD 的核心 selection 结果 (LP +1.36 pp) 添加 2-3 seed replication；或者在 Limitations 中更明确指出 selection 结果的 seed coverage 比 QE 更有限。

### [Should-Fix] W6: Few-NERD 训练配置差异未充分讨论

- **位置**: Appendix L ("3 epochs" for Few-NERD vs. 5 epochs for SciERC/CoNLL)
- **问题**: Few-NERD 仅训练 3 epochs（vs. 其他数据集的 5 epochs），这可能直接导致 lower degeneracy（更少训练 → 更弱模型 → 更多 diversity）。如果 Few-NERD 的低 degeneracy 部分源自 under-training 而非数据集固有特性，则 degeneracy-selection 关系的因果方向被混淆。
- **论文在 Discussion 中提到** "dataset-specific factors (number of entity types, semantic overlap) also modulate the rate"，但没有排除 training epoch 差异这一 confound。
- **建议**: 在 appendix 中添加 epoch sensitivity 分析（如 Few-NERD 5 epoch 的 degeneracy rate），或明确讨论为何使用 3 epochs（early stopping? 收敛?）。

### [Minor] W7: Soft Jaccard 分母选择的 claim 缺乏完整表达

- **位置**: Section 3.2, Equation 4, footnote
- **问题**: 论文声称 max vs union normalizer 差异 Δρ<0.01，并在 Appendix (Table 5) 给出了 6 个 model-dataset combinations 的证据。这实际上是充分的。但 footnote 的表述 "nearly identical rankings (Δρ<0.01; Table X)" 暗示这是所有条件下的 bound，而表中最大差异是 0.009——距 0.01 仅一个量级，更准确的表述是 "|Δρ| ��� 0.009"。
- **建议**: 微调措辞精度即可。

### [Minor] W8: Table 3 与 Table 4 的 greedy F1 不一致可能困惑读者

- **位置**: Table 3 (SciERC greedy=0.645), Table 4 (SciERC greedy=0.614)
- **问题**: 两表使用不同 evaluation protocol (gold-filtered n=529 vs. full-set n=551)，导致同一模型的 greedy F1 差 3.1 pp。虽然 Table 4 有脚注解释，但读者在主文中连续看到两个不同的 baseline 数字时容易困惑。
- **建议**: 统一 evaluation protocol，或在 Table 4 同时报告 gold-filtered 数字。

---

## Questions (需要作者澄清)

**Q1**: Section 4.5 LoRA rank=8 ablation 中，LP 的 median within-instance range 是多少？如果 rank=8 下 LP range 显著小于 rank=32 下的 0.041 nats，则 selection failure 可归因于更严重的 compression 而非 degeneracy 本身不充分���

**Q2**: Few-NERD 训练为何仅 3 epochs？是否有 early stopping 或 validation loss plateau 的证据？5 epochs 下的 degeneracy rate 是多少？

**Q3**: Table 3 的 sign test 使用的是 instance-level 配对（对每个 instance 比较 LP-selected F1 vs greedy F1），还是 corpus-level 比较？如果是 instance-level，n=529 × 2 seeds = 1058 paired observations 应该有更强的 power。

**Q4**: Within-instance SJ-F1 ρ=0.52 (Section 5) 报告为 median；distribution 如何？有多少比例的 non-degenerate instances 有 ρ<0？如果大量 instances 的 within-instance correlation 为负或接近零，则 "well-aligned utility" 的 claim 需要 qualify。

## Missing References

1. **Best-of-N with process reward models**: Lightman et al. (2024) "Let's Verify Step by Step" 在 math reasoning 中展示了 verifier-based BoN 的 scaling law——与本文"需要 learned verifier"的结论直接相关，已引用但可更深入对比。
2. **Self-consistency for structured prediction beyond NER**: Yoran et al. (2023) "Answering Questions by Meta-Reasoning over Multiple Chains of Thought" 和 Li et al. (2023) "Making Language Models Better Reasoners with Step-Aware Verifier" 在 structured reasoning 中有类似 gap 的发现。
3. **Diversity in fine-tuned models**: Zhang et al. (2024) "Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters" (DeepMind) 讨论了 fine-tuned model 的 diversity collapse 与 test-time compute 的关系——直接相关。
4. **MBR for structured prediction**: Eikema et al. (2025) "Structured MBR" 已引用但可更详细讨论为何 IE 的 bag-of-unit mismatch 比 MT 更严重。

---

### Abstract
- 信息密度高，四个必答问题都有覆盖。
- "correlation-selection gap" 概念在 Abstract 中引入但未定义（主文 Section 4.3 才定义），建议用一句简短释义。
- 数字选择合理（ρ, AUROC, pp gains, p values）。

- 叙事线清晰：从 self-consistency 的成功切入 NER 的结构性挑战。

- 数据集选择合理且角色分工清晰。
- 训练细节 (Appendix E, Table 7) 充分：LoRA config、optimizer、batch size、epoch 均报告。
- vLLM + XGrammar constrained decoding 描述清楚；但 vLLM 版本号未报告（影响 reproducibility）。

### Discussion (Section 5)
- 这一节承载了大量 ablation 和 diagnostic 结果，密度极高。
- Entity-token LP ablation 的 negative result 是好的：排除了 format-token dilution 作为 primary cause。
- Signal combination 失败（logistic regression、MLP、RF）有力支撑了 "feature space bottleneck" 的结论。
- "Practical considerations" 段落实用价值高（N=8 suffices for QE, cost-benefit for selection is unfavorable）。

### Limitations
- 全面且诚实（scale limitation、seed coverage、untested verifier、ε post-hoc choice）。
- 建议补充: power analysis limitation、Few-NERD epoch confound。

Reviewer 2 raises several interesting points. Let me go through each one systematically, comparing against what I found in the paper during my own review. I need to provide [AGREE] or [REBUT] for each weakness and question, citing specific evidence from the paper.

Let me think through each:

**W1**: "correlation-selection gap" novelty is limited - repackaging of known observations.
- The claim that instance-level signals can't rank per-sample is indeed trivial by definition. The paper acknowledges this.
- Diversity collapse is known (Kirk et al. 2024 is cited).
- But the COMBINATION and the systematic empirical demonstration across a difficulty gradient IS new. 

The paper's real contribution is synthesizing these known pieces into a unified framework specifically for structured IE, supported by empirical evidence across different difficulty levels. I partially agree the novelty lies in the demonstration and framing rather than individual observations, but I'd push back on calling it pure repackaging.

**W2**: Degeneracy as model success, not failure mechanism.
- This is a sharp observation. CoNLL's 58% degeneracy with 91% F1 suggests the model is simply performing well. Few-NERD's 10% degeneracy with 75% F1 indicates less convergence.
- The Few-NERD results actually support the paper's point here—the lower degeneracy correlates with lower performance, which contradicts the idea that degeneracy is just a sign of success.
- The 4B vs 8B comparison on SciERC is particularly telling: both models achieve similar performance (~65% F1) but show very different degeneracy rates (10.4% vs 21%), suggesting model size and dataset characteristics matter independently of performance.
- I think the paper has stronger evidence here than R2's framing acknowledges.

**W3**: No positive contribution.
- Fair criticism for a top-tier venue, since the paper is purely diagnostic. That said, negative or diagnostic results do get accepted at *ACL conferences when they reveal something meaningful about how methods fail or behave.
- The paper does offer some actionable takeaways—using quality estimation signals rather than selection, and recognizing that loss-based pruning works better in low-degeneracy settings—though I'd agree it's borderline for main conference standards.

**W4**: Excessive em-dashes and AI-like writing style.
- This is a presentation issue rather than a scientific one, but if there really are ~90 em-dashes throughout, it does affect readability and professionalism.

**W5**: Abstract is too number-dense.
- Valid stylistic concern; the Abstract packs in too many metrics and makes it harder to extract the main message.

**W6**: Differentiation from Yao et al. (2026).
- The Related Work does address this—Yao et al. focus on consistency-accuracy tradeoffs in hard-prompting, while this paper extends to fine-tuned models, separates quality estimation from selection, and diagnoses failure modes. The distinction exists but could be articulated more clearly.

**W7**: Missing Byerly & Khashabi (2024) reference.
- I'm not familiar with this paper, so I can't verify if it's real or hallucinated. I'll be cautious about taking a strong stance here.

**W8**: Discussion section is overstuffed.
- I see the density—it covers many ablations—but most of the content feels necessary. Some material on signal combinations and practical considerations could shift to the appendix.

**Q1**: Output space size as a driver of degeneracy.
- That's a compelling hypothesis. Few-NERD has 8 entity types while CoNLL has 4, so larger type inventories create more possible entity configurations and make identical outputs less likely. The paper does touch on this in Section 5 when mentioning entity types and semantic overlap as modulators.

**Q2**: The LoRA rank=8 case shows 7% degeneracy but selection still fails.
- This points to the same underlying tension.

The paper's "necessary but not sufficient" framing holds up with this data, though the confounds I flagged earlier—LP compression persisting across conditions—mean the ablation doesn't cleanly isolate degeneracy as the sole factor.

**Q3**: Larger models show higher degeneracy.
- That's a legitimate concern, but the paper acknowledges it as an open question rather than claiming their findings scale universally.

**Q4**: A supervised verifier with richer token-level features would be more powerful.
- True, the current verifier relies on just five scalar signals, which is a real limitation of the diagnostic approach. Though the paper frames this as testing whether information exists in those specific signals rather than building an optimal verifier.

# Reviewer 1 交叉回应 — 对 Reviewer 2 审稿意见逐条回应

---

## Weaknesses 回应

**[REBUT] R2-W1: "Correlation-selection gap" 新颖性有限**

R2 称三层诊断是已知 observation 的 repackaging。我部分不同意：

(1) "Instance-level signals 不能做 per-sample ranking 是 trivial by definition" — 表面上 trivial，但 prior work（Yao et al. 2026; Vashurin et al. 2025 CoCoA; Taubenfeld et al. 2025 CISC）直接用 consistency signals 做 selection，说明社区并未普遍认识到这一区分。论文 Section 1 第二段明确指出 "Prior work on confidence estimation for LLM-based IE has conflated quality estimation with sample selection"。如果是 trivial，这些 prior work 不应该存在。

(2) "Diversity collapse 是已知现象" — Kirk et al. (2024) 讨论的是 RLHF 下的 diversity collapse 作为 alignment tax；本文的 instance degeneracy 是 supervised fine-tuning 下的量化现象，且关键贡献不在于发现 degeneracy 存在，而在于量化其与 selection headroom 的具体关系（Table 5: 21% constant F1 + 13% constant utility = 34% instances 完全没有 selection room）。

(3) 但我同意 R2 关于 "是否构成 EMNLP 主会议长文贡献量" 的质疑。纯诊断性 negative result 论文需要很强的 insight density。论文在 diagnostic depth 上做到了，但缺乏 constructive output 确实限制了贡献的完整性。

**结论**: 不同意 "repackaging" 的定性，但同意 contribution 量对 main conference 偏弱，可能更适合 Findings。

---

**[REBUT] R2-W2: Degeneracy = model success 的 natural consequence**

R2 的逻辑是：CoNLL 58% degeneracy ← 91% F1（好模型），Few-NERD 10% ← 75% F1（弱模型），因此 degeneracy 仅反映 model quality。

但论文有两个直接反驳：

(a) **Few-NERD 75% F1 + 10% degeneracy vs. SciERC 66% F1 + 21% degeneracy** (Table 4, Section 5): Few-NERD 性能更高但 degeneracy 更低。如果 degeneracy 纯粹是 model quality 的函数，这一反转不应出现。论文在 Section 5 明确讨论："Few-NERD's low degeneracy despite high performance suggests that dataset-specific factors (number of entity types, semantic overlap) also modulate the rate。"

(b) **4B vs 8B on SciERC** (Table 5): 8B degeneracy 21% vs 4B degeneracy 10.4%，但 within-instance utility correlation 可比 (ρ=0.52 vs 0.55)。这证明 degeneracy 不仅是 accuracy 的 proxy——更高能力的模型在相同任务上产生更多 degeneracy，即使 within-instance 的 quality 分布仍有结构。

R2 的简化 ("LP selection only works when the model is bad enough") 与 Few-NERD 数据矛盾：Few-NERD 是 75% F1（不差），LP 仍然 work (+1.36 pp)。

**但我同意** R2 的 deeper point：论文需要更清楚地 disentangle degeneracy 的多个 driver（model quality, output space size, schema complexity, training epochs），而非将其作为一个 monolithic "mechanism"。这与我在 W1 中提出的 concern 一致。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W3: 缺乏可操作的 positive contribution**

同意。论文唯一的 constructive suggestion 是 "需要 trained verifiers"（Section 5 最后段, Conclusion 最后句），但自己没有实现。Entity-token LP remedy 失败（Section 5 entity-token LP ablation），supervised verifier baseline 也失败 (Section 4.5)。LP + VC 组合全部失败 (Section 5 "Signal combinations")。

对于 EMNLP main conference，我认为至少需要以下之一来补偿：
- 一个 working (哪怕 partial) verifier baseline 展示 oracle gap 可以被 partially closed
- 或者一个 clear actionable framework 告诉 practitioner exactly when to use BoN（例如基于 degeneracy rate 的 decision rule）

论文在 practical considerations 段落有一些 guidance，但不够 concrete to be actionable。

不过我注意到：Few-NERD 的 LP selection 成功 (+1.36 pp, p<0.001) 本身就是 positive result，只是论文将其 framing 为 diagnostic evidence 而非 practical method。如果 reframe 为 "LP selection works in the low-degeneracy regime, and we characterize when that regime occurs"，practical value 会更明显。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W4: em-dash 过度使用**

同意这是一个 presentation quality 问题。我没有专门计数，但通读全文时确实注意到频繁的 em-dash 使用（特别是在 Discussion section）。按照 ACL 写作规范和审稿人期望，减少 em-dash 使用是低成本高收益的修改。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W5: Abstract 和 Introduction 数字堆��**

同意。我重新检查 Abstract：在约 180 words 中有 "ρ up to 0.38", "0.42", "AUROC up to 0.82", "~13 pp", "ρ=0.52", "10-58%", "0.041 nats", "+1.36 pp", "p<0.001", "58%", "+0.42 pp", "$N=8$ to 16", "p=0.003" — 密度过高。这是 experimental report 风格而非 story-driven 叙事。每个数字单独看是 justified，但整体上牺牲了可读性。

---

**[REBUT] R2-W6: 与 Yao et al. (2026) 差异化不足**

论文在 Section 1 第二段（Introduction）和 Section 2 "Consistency for structured IE" 段落中明确列出差异：(1) Yao et al. 使用 hard-prompting，本文使用 fine-tuned models（degeneracy 更严重）；(2) Yao et al. 仅报告 correlation，未区分 QE vs selection；(3) 本文诊断了两个具体 failure mechanisms。

差异化实际上是充分的——Table 4 的 Few-NERD 结果和 Section 4.5 的 LoRA ablation 都是 Yao et al. 不覆盖的实验。但 Introduction 中差异化的叙述方式可以更 upfront（目前在第二段中间，容易被跳过）。

---

**[REBUT] R2-W7: Missing reference Byerly & Khashabi (2024) "Self-Consistency Falls Short"**

我无法确认这篇论文存在。在我的知识范围内，没有 Byerly & Khashabi (2024) 以这个确切标题发表的论文。如果 R2 能提供确切 venue 或 arXiv ID，我可以重新评估。建议作者在 rebuttal 中 verify 这一引用的存在性。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W8: Discussion 过长**

同意。Discussion (Section 5) 承载了：(1) practical implications, (2) why the gap exists (degeneracy + LP compression analysis), (3) non-tied subset analysis, (4) N-scaling effect, (5) temperature effect, (6) verbalized confidence, (7) signal combinations, (8) LP compression hypotheses, (9) free-form ablation, (10) entity-token LP, (11) pilot remedy, (12) practical considerations, (13) regime boundaries, (14) methodological implications. 这是 14 个 distinct sub-topics 在一个 section 中。

建议：将 (3) non-tied subset, (4) N-scaling, (5) temperature, (6) verbalized confidence, (7) signal combinations 移入 Appendix，仅在 Discussion 保留引用。这可释放 ~1 page 空间用于 constructive contribution。

---

## Minor Issues 回应

**[AGREE] R2-M1**: "leverage" 用词问题——Minor，容易修复。

**[REBUT] R2-M2**: Abstract 中 NER 需定义——NER (Named Entity Recognition) 是 NLP 社区的标准缩写，ARR 审稿人不需要定义。MBR 可能确实需要定义或避免在 Abstract 中使��（Abstract 中首次出现 "MBR / consensus-proximity selection" 在 line 6，未展开）。

**[AGREE] R2-M3**: Table 3 EM/VC 无 p 值——同意需要解释。查看 Table 3，EM (0.637) 和 VC (0.623) 明显低于 greedy (0.645)，因此方向为负，paired test 不会给 "improvement" p 值。但论文应标注 "—" 并注释 "below greedy, test not applicable"。

**[AGREE] R2-M4**: Figure 3 "~15%" 的定义——确实不精确。Dashed line 位置应有 explicit justification（如来自 ROC 分析或 breakpoint detection），而非视觉近似。

**[REBUT] R2-M5**: em-dash vs en-dash 区分——这是排版规范问题，不影响科学内容。论文使用 LaTeX `---` (em-dash) 用于解释性插入。按 ACL style guide，em-dash 本身不违规，只是频率过高（同意 W4）。

---

## Questions 回应

**[AGREE] R2-Q1: Output space size 驱动 degeneracy**

这是一个重要的 alternative explanation。Few-NERD 8 types vs CoNLL 4 types 意味着可能的 entity set configurations 指数级更多，自然降低 exact match degeneracy。论文在 Section 5 提到 "number of entity types" 作为 modulating factor，但未做 controlled analysis。

这与我在 W1 中的 concern 一致：degeneracy 可能主要是 output space size 的函数，而非独立的 "mechanism"。如果在 CoNLL 上增加 entity types（如 fine-grained NER），degeneracy 可能也会下降——那么 "degeneracy gates selection" 本质上就是 "output space diversity gates selection"，这个 framing 更准确但也更 trivial。

---

**[AGREE] R2-Q2: LoRA rank=8 证据对 degeneracy-as-gating-factor 的挑战**

完全同意。这与我在 W2 中的分析一致：rank=8 下 degeneracy 7.2% 但 LP selection 仍失败，直接挑战了 "degeneracy is the gating factor" 的 framing。论文的 "necessary but not sufficient" 回应在逻辑上成立，但实验设计上混淆了 degeneracy 下降和模型能力下降这两个变量。

---

**[REBUT] R2-Q3: 70B+ 模型是否使 research direction 无望**

不同意 "无望" 的暗示。两个理由：

(a) 70B+ 模型可能有更强的 LP signal quality（representation space 更丰富），即使 degeneracy 更高。LP compression 可能在 larger models 中有不同 pattern——论文未测试不代表方向无望。

(b) 更重要的是，论文的 QE contribution 不受 degeneracy 影响——即使 70B 模型 degeneracy 更高，QE signals 仍然有用（selective prediction, error flagging）。只是 selection 方向可能确实在 highly capable models 上受限。

论文在 Limitations 中诚实承认这一未知："Whether the gap holds for 70B+ models is untested—larger models may produce more diverse samples." 这是合理的 scope limitation 而非 fatal flaw。

---

**[AGREE] R2-Q4: Supervised verifier 仅用 5 scalar features**

同意这是 verifier experiment 的主要局限。5 个 scalar features（all are instance-level aggregates except LP）本身就 encode 不了 per-sample discriminative information——这几乎是 set up to fail。

如果加入 token-level features（如 per-entity log-prob, attention entropy, hidden state uncertainty），verifier 可能表现完全不同。Section 4.5 的 supervised verifier 结论 ("bottleneck lies in the feature space") 实际上只能说 "bottleneck lies in THESE specific 5 features"，不能泛化为 "no feature combination can close the gap"。

但我也注意到��论文 frame 这个实验的目的是 "test whether the information bottleneck lies in the aggregation method or the features themselves"——在这个 narrow claim 下，实验设计是合理的（固定 features，变 aggregation method）。只是 broader conclusion 需要 qualify。

---

## 总结性评价

R2 的核心 concern（novelty/contribution 量不足 for main conference）是合理的，但部分 technical criticisms（W2 的 degeneracy = model success 简化）在论文数据面前不完全成立。我认为论文的贡献介于 Main Conference 和 Findings 之间：

- **支撑 Main Conference 的因素**: 实验系统性、统计严谨性、三层诊断的清晰度、Few-NERD positive result
- **支撑 Findings 的因素**: 缺乏 constructive contribution (W3)、核心因果 claim 证据偏薄 (与我的 W1-W2 一致)、novelty 主要在 framing 而非 new method

我维持 **Borderline Accept (3.5/5)** 的评分，但认为 R2 的 **Borderline Reject (3/5)** 也在合���范围内。关键分歧在于 "purely diagnostic paper with strong execution" 是否 sufficient for main conference。
